articles.title: Eagles sink Cowboys with historic NFL Thanksgiving comeback
articles.summary: Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left as the Philadelphia Eagles produced a staggering 21-point comeback to beat the Dallas Cowboys 39-38 in a Thanksgiving epic on Thursday.
body: Joe Milton throws three touchdown passes while DeVonta Smith records 200 receiving yards as the Philadelphia Eagles deliver the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving Day history to shock the Dallas Cowboys in a 39-38 victory.

Dallas had led by as many as 21 points in the third quarter only to see ever-reliable kicker Brandon Aubrey miss a 40-yard field goal before the Eagles pulled to within two, down 38-36 with two minutes remaining.

Dak Prescott was then sacked by Ty Johnson on fourth-and-one with 55 seconds left before Markquese Bell gifted the Eagles a first down with a pass interference penalty on third-and-one on the ensuing possession.
It would eventually tee up Elliott's crowning moment as he kicked the Eagles to the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history.

articles.title: Europa League: Bournemouth make it a perfect 10 while Celtic leave it late
articles.summary: Marco Rose’s team close in on qualification. Marseille v Levski Sofia marred by crowd trouble. Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo.
body: It was a remarkable 10th victory in succession in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time.
The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafodé Diakité was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.

Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Álvaro Rodríguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half. A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time. Rose’s team could secure a top-eight finish and a last-16 berth when they host Viktoria Plzen, 4-0 winners over Benfica, in two weeks’ time.
Camilo Durán came to Celtic ’s rescue in Europe again after coming off the bench to head a late winner against Torreense in Portugal.

articles.title: Reinildo error extends Sunderland woe as Jagiellonia grab Europa League draw
articles.summary: Jagiellonia Bialystok’s head coach, Adrian Siemieniec, claimed this trip to Wearside to face Premier League opposition represented one of the biggest highlights of a career in which he has already celebrated a Polish title.
body: His players did everything to guarantee it was not an anticlimax as they revelled in highlighting Sunderland’s struggles in front of goal courtesy of some intelligent defending. Along the way they also responded to falling behind with an almost immediate equaliser and forced the impressive Robin Roefs into the evening’s more taxing saves.

It leaves Régis Le Bris’ team 13th in the Europa League table before their trip to Milan in two weeks’ time. If the playoffs remain well within reach, Sunderland’s hopes of automatic progress to the knockout phase are fading and a smattering of boos greeted the final whistle.
“Frustrating game,” said Le Bris, who, with one eye on Sunday’s Premier League game against Spurs here, rotated his starting XI. “It was a well deserved point for the opponent.”
The eastern Polish city of Bialystok lies close to the Belarusian and Lithuanian borders but the arduous journey to north-east England was not responsible for the lack of Jagiellonia fans.

articles.title: Australia's sandpapergate probe to also include 2017-18 Ashes
articles.summary: Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England.
body: The terms of reference for the independent forum have been published and the scope will include "ball-management practices in the Australian men's team during the 2017–18 season", which includes the Ashes series Australia won 4-0.
Also included are all four Tests of the subsequent South Africa tour and the investigation which followed when the ball-tampering scandal emerged.
Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report and recommendations within 30 days of receiving them.
All those involved in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa will be invited to speak to the independent forum, though none will have to do so and no retrospective sanctions will be handed out.

articles.title: Hearts' European hopes hang by a thread but Vrancken proud
articles.summary: Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken expresses both pride and disappointment after his team came out on the wrong side of a five-goal thriller against Monaco.
body: There was a bittersweet feeling at Tynecastle after Folarin Balogun's 94th-minute winner preserved Monaco's perfect Conference League record and condemned Hearts to a third defeat from four.
Wouter Vrancken's side had gone toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the tournament, scored two glorious goals, but ultimately came away with nothing for their efforts.
Now they have little to no margin for error in their two remaining league phase matches.

They will likely have to beat both Borac Banja Luka of Bosnia and Cyprus' Pafos to reach the knockout stages, but if they perform as they did against Monaco, they will give themselves a fighting chance.

articles.title: Vrancken proud of Hearts players despite last-gasp defeat to Monaco
articles.summary: Wouter Vrancken expressed pride in his Hearts team after an agonising 3-2 defeat at home to Monaco left their Conference League hopes hanging by a thread.
body: The Jambos looked on course to pick up their second league-phase point after stunning first-half strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota either side of goals from visiting pair Folarin Balogun and Edian Diop.

But in the fourth and final minute of added time, injury-hit Hearts were denied what would have been a hugely commendable result when USA forward Balogun found space in the box to slot home and maintain Monaco's perfect record in the competition.

"The biggest thing is, of course, to be really proud of the performance we put on the park today, because it's against a really good side," said Vrancken, keen to reiterate that his team remains without several key players.
"Knowing that we have still nine injuries, I will mention it, and we have a lot of players not on the European list today and to still do this against that team, I'm really proud of what we did."

articles.title: Bakole: Late-notice Wilder fight not like Parker | 'I like danger!'
articles.summary: Martin Bakole explained his decision to step in as a replacement opponent for Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard next month.
body: After Jai Opetaia withdrew from his December 11 bout with former heavyweight world champion Wilder, Bakole came in to take his place on the Principality Stadium bill.
He insists it is a very different scenario to his short-notice assignment against Joseph Parker last year.
Bakole came in to box Parker for the WBO Interim title, landing in Riyadh just a day before the fight. Parker promptly put him down heavily and stopped him in their second round.
For this fight with Wilder though he's had more warning. He was training in Las Vegas to box on the same bill, albeit originally for a much lower-level opponent.

articles.title: Bears stun Lions, Eagles rally in NFL Thanksgiving thrillers
articles.summary: Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a game-winning touchdown with three seconds remaining on Thursday as the Chicago Bears beat the Detroit Lions 39-35 in an NFL Thanksgiving holiday thriller.
body: Williams's six-yard pass to Odunze -- who managed to get both feet down in the back corner of the end zone -- gave the Bears their first lead of the game in Detroit, where victory lifted them to 9-2 and into the NFC North division lead over the 8-3 Lions.
"We knew we needed a big one," Odunze said. "Luckily the O-line held up for me. Caleb delivered the ball exactly where it needed to be, and I was able to make a play in the back of the end zone."
Williams connected on 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns -- both to Odunze.
The Bears had two rushing touchdowns from Kyle Monangai and one from D'Andre Swift to help offset a monster game from Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who ran for 205 yards and three TDs.

articles.title: How Joe Milton may have secured next contract with 'revenge' Thanksgiving performance vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Not long ago, Milton was a backup to Dak Prescott. On Thanksgiving, he beat his former team with a thrilling four-touchdown performance — the kind of win that could give him further contract looks in the future.
body: How Joe Milton may have secured next contract with 'revenge' Thanksgiving performance vs. Cowboys originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Everybody around the NFL has known since Joe Milton entered the league that he has the arm to succeed in the pros. But until Thursday, he hadn't yet put it all together in a starting role.

Last month, Milton was signed to the Eagles ' active roster off the Cowboys ' practice squad following Jalen Hurts' season-ending blood clot issue. Fast forward a few weeks, and he was torching Dallas' defense in a comeback win for Philadelphia on the Thanksgiving stage.
With his four-touchdown performance against his former team, Milton may have earned himself his next NFL contract — and potentially even future consideration as a starter.
